reason: The passage depicts Yahweh as protective and supportive of the Hebrew people, specifically David. Yahweh prevents David from committing violence (מְנָעֲךָ יְהוָה מִבּוֹא בְדָמִים - 'the Lord held you back from coming to bloody deeds'), promises to establish David's house (בַּיִת נֶאֱמָן), fights Israel's battles through David (מִלְחֲמוֹת יְהוָה אֲדֹנִי נִלְחָם), and strikes down Nabal who was antagonistic to David (וַיִּגֹּף יְהוָה אֶת־ נָבָל וַיָּמֹת). The entire narrative demonstrates Yahweh's favor and protection of His people.
